options.name: Flow Velocity
options.description: Flow velocity defines the magnitude and direction of fluid movement at an inlet, outlet, or other flow boundary in an Icepak model. It is used to represent forced-air cooling conditions produced by fans, blowers, or an external airflow source. This parameter is important because airflow transports heat away from components and influences the development of the thermal and pressure fields. An inappropriate velocity definition can produce unrealistic convection, component temperatures, or flow distribution. The value and direction should therefore be selected from the actual boundary condition, system airflow information, or validated test data rather than from a universal recommended value.

options.name: Radiation Model
options.description: The radiation model determines how thermal energy exchanged by electromagnetic radiation between surfaces is represented in an Icepak simulation. It becomes important when surface temperatures, emissivity, view relationships, or low-convection environments make radiative heat transfer significant. Enabling an appropriate radiation model can improve the prediction of component and enclosure temperatures, but it may also increase model setup requirements and computational cost. An unsuitable model or inaccurate surface properties can distort the calculated heat balance. The selection should therefore consider the physical environment, surface properties, expected temperature levels, and the required balance between simulation accuracy and solution time.
